answer: A mechanism that actually bites: attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because bridge only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, beacon is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any pigment approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
